claims.text: Tungsten-carbide-based cermet coatings significantly reduce molten-aluminum corrosion of steel rollers.
Tungsten-carbide-based cermet coatings extend the service life of steel rollers relative to uncoated rollers in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
HVOF thermal spraying can be used to apply a tungsten-carbide-based cermet coating to steel roller substrates.
Typical molten-aluminum temperatures in the proposed hot-dip plating application are approximately 680–750°C.
The coating will produce a dense cermet layer on the steel surface.
The cermet layer will adhere to the steel substrate during service.
The dense, adherent cermet layer limits chemical interaction between molten aluminum and the steel surface.
The cermet layer limits mechanical wear caused by molten aluminum.
The tungsten-carbide-based cermet is chemically stable in molten aluminum under the stated conditions.
The hardness of the cermet contributes to resistance against wear.
The cermet coating acts as a barrier that prevents aluminum infiltration into the steel substrate.
Tungsten-carbide-coated rollers will have significantly lower mass loss than uncoated steel rollers under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
The coating will provide a two- to threefold increase in roller service life relative to uncoated steel rollers.
Uncoated steel rollers typically undergo rapid mass loss and premature failure because of corrosion and erosion in molten aluminum.
Suboptimal coating application quality may reduce the coating's performance gains.
Thermal or shock cycling beyond recommended cermet-coating limits may reduce performance gains.
The degree of service-life extension depends on coating thickness, substrate preparation, and operating parameters.
